headline_findings: ITEM 13 — the request storm is a STALLED /api/flow/version, not a remount and not a render gate. In 4 of 5 storms, picks-mount time tracks the version request's duration almost exactly. The legacy-tape fallback it triggers serves a STALE version every time.

ITEM 12 — every one of the 7 large handoffs reports blocked_by=null, so the ledger cannot explain its own worst cases. api/flow_router.py's comment asserting that blocked_by 'is the whole explanation for a large one' is falsified by today's data. Named candidate: blocked_by is snapshotted AT SIGHTING, so a holder that takes the slot immediately after is invisible forever.

ITEM 14 — Search cannot build its product for NVDA or MU during RTH. Both blow a 20 s warm budget (27.2 s / 21.3 s), the work is discarded, and a 600 s cooldown means retrying cannot help. Two of the three head names are permanently on the slow legacy path.

ITEM 8 — the improvement is real but much smaller than a naive read gives. Filed at n=60 it was -46.2%; at n=89 it is -30.2%; the steady-state plateau is -12.9%. Same session, same flag, different stopping point.
ITEM 11 — warm re-entry beats UCT20 on commits and LOSES on bytes by roughly an order of magnitude once dwell-time polling is controlled for.
ITEM 15 / A1 — another workstream pushed to master at 09:27 ET and members saw 502s for ~45 s across the market open.
corrections_made_during_the_run: loganalyze.py first classified /api/flow/aggregate-health as a whole-D request, counting THIS SESSION'S OWN poller as 15 member whole-D calls. Fixed before item 7 was filed; had it stood, item 7 would have reported a 65% member whole-D ratio that was entirely my own instrument.
item 4 was first written with bucket_bound_s: null on rolls 6-10 — my transcription, not a reading. Re-read from the samples and corrected; all ten carry values.
item 12 was first filed at n=55 claiming the handoff distribution had a COMPLETELY empty middle. At n=89 one roll (2046 ms) sits in 501-5000 ms. Corrected in place, first pass retained.

item 8 was first filed at n=60 with a -46.2% headline. Corrected to -30.2% at n=89 and to -12.9% on the plateau, with both earlier passes retained because the spread between them is itself the finding.

item 14: I formed two hypotheses for why NVDA/MU never warmed (lock starvation; a version-keyed cache treadmill) and BOTH were wrong. declined=0 and a per-symbol freshness key ruled them out; the server log gave the real cause.
known_gaps: item 1: 'no overnight tracebacks' and 'T+1 flat-file backfill completed' are UNEVALUATED — `railway logs` returns a capped ~500-line / ~1-hour buffer and there is no overnight window to read.
item 7: no member traffic existed, so parts-vs-whole-D has no denominator. Marked inconclusive, not passed.
items 9 and 10: runs were issued back-to-back rather than deliberately phased against the ~60 s roll cycle. Phase coverage was incidental.
item 9: the intro animation's share is DERIVED by differencing path A and path B, not measured — the rig exposes no intro-duration field.
item 11: no recorded weekend figures exist to regress against; both sides were measured fresh today. The byte comparison does not cleanly isolate navigation cost (control batch included).

item 13: run 11 stormed with a FAST version request and is unexplained by the version-stall mechanism; run 4's 32 s stall has no matching server-side handoff. At least one more path into the storm shape exists.
item 15 / A3: stale_served is a server counter my own rig also increments; I did not separate my share, so the absolute 98 is not member impact.
csv_provider share (asked for by items 4 and 8) is NOT EXPOSED anywhere in /api/flow/aggregate-health.

evidence_files.web-log-stream.jsonl: same for web. Contains NO HTTP access lines — web logs only scheduler/app output, which is why item 7 had to use flow-worker's log.
